How does SSM Patch Manager work?

Patch Manager automates OS, application, and security patching of EC2 and on-premises instances, on Linux, macOS, and Windows. A Patch Baseline defines the approved or rejected patches; instances are attached to a Patch Group through the Patch Group tag, itself registered with a single baseline. The patching runs with the AWS-RunPatchBaseline document via Run Command, on demand or in a Maintenance Window with Rate Control. A compliance report lists the missing patches and can be sent to S3.

It is a scheduled window for running actions on instances: patching, driver updates, software installation. It contains a schedule, a duration, registered targets, and registered tasks. Rate Control is used there to limit the number or percentage of targets working in parallel.
Why prefer Session Manager over SSH?

Session Manager requires no SSH access, no bastion, and no SSH keys: access goes through IAM via console, CLI, or SDK. No inbound rule is needed in the Security Group. Connections and commands are logged to S3 or CloudWatch Logs, and CloudTrail records StartSession. You can restrict access by tags, and even limit the allowed commands.
Putting an instance in several Patch Groups: impossible, one instance = a single Patch Group.
Forgetting the exact tag key "Patch Group": without it the instance receives the default baseline.
Believing that a predefined baseline can be modified: only a custom baseline can.
Thinking that Session Manager requires port 22 to be open: the agent initiates an outbound connection.
Forgetting to configure session logs: without an S3/CloudWatch destination, no command history.

AWS-RunPatchBaseline applies the OS and application patches.
